newsitem.title: BURUNDI: 37 killed south of Burundian capital - sources.
newsitem.headline: 37 killed south of Burundian capital - sources.

text.p: Thirty-seven people were killed on Friday in fighting south of Bujumbura, the capital of Burundi, witnesses and opposition sources said on Monday.
Military spokesman Isaie Nibizi said the army carried out a military operation in the area for most of last week after rebels armed with machineguns and mortars were sighted there.
He said two soldiers and several rebels were killed in the fighting, near Mutunea, 20 km (12 miles) from the capital.
The witnesses said many of the 37 were killed by mortar rounds fired by the army but Colonel Nibizi denied this.
The main rebel group is the ethnic Hutu Forces for the Defence of Democracy (FDD), which is trying to overthrow the Tutsi-dominated government in power since a coup in July.
The rebels said on Sunday they were engaging army positions in five main regions of the central African nation and fierce fighting was sending refugees streaming into Tanzania.

But a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency in the western Tanzanian town of Kigoma told Reuters by telephone that only 950 fresh refugees had arrived in Tanzania on Saturday, although he pointed out that it took refugees between four days to a week to reach the neighbouring east African country.
